# round2_q2: partial answer

## Proved: Step 1 (devissage) for fine P

**Structure of B_P.** Let P be fine. Every face of P is generated by finitely many elements, so it is the face spanned by one element x (take the sum of the generators). For faces Phi(x), Phi(x'), there is a morphism P[-x]^sharp -> P[-x']^sharp under P exactly when x maps to a unit in P[-x']^sharp. Because P[-x']^sharp is sharp, this means x maps to 0, i.e. x lies in Phi(x'). Such a morphism is unique, by the universal property. So B_P is equivalent to the finite poset Faces(P), ordered by inclusion. A presheaf F on B_P^op is a covariant functor on this poset: there are maps F(Phi) -> F(Phi') when Phi ⊂ Phi'. The smallest face {0} corresponds to P.

**Filtration.** Let U be an upward-closed set of faces. Define F_U to equal F on U and 0 elsewhere. This is a subfunctor of F: a transition map leaving U would have to go downward, which is impossible, so all transition maps out of U stay in U. List the faces in a linear extension Phi_1, ..., Phi_r of the order, starting with the largest. The sets U_k = {Phi_1, ..., Phi_k} are upward closed. They give a finite filtration 0 = F_{U_0} ⊂ ... ⊂ F_{U_r} = F. Each graded piece F_{U_k}/F_{U_{k-1}} is concentrated at the single face Phi_k, with value F(Phi_k), and is again a functor on B_P^op.

**Reduction.** pi^{-1} is exact: it is the left adjoint of a geometric morphism, and the inclusion is left exact. R pi_* is a triangulated functor. So F -> R pi_* pi^{-1} F is a natural transformation between exact functors on bounded complexes. By induction along the filtration, using the five lemma on the long exact sequences, it is a quasi-isomorphism for every F if it is one for every F concentrated at a single face. By R0, it is enough to check H^*(A_P, pi^{-1} F) for such F, for all fine P.

## Not proved

- **Step 2 (P = N^2).** I did not do the computation. Its key ingredient is the claimed description of the neighbourhoods of rank-two valuations in background item R5. I have not verified that description.
- **Step 3 (general fine P).** Not done.

## Open

The remaining lemma, still open, is this. For fine P and F concentrated at a single face Phi with value A:
- H^0(A_P, pi^{-1}F) = A if Phi = {0}, and 0 otherwise;
- H^i(A_P, pi^{-1}F) = 0 for all i > 0.

So the headline question is unresolved. The expected answer is YES, but this file proves only the reduction above.
